candidate.title: Safe-SeqS
candidate.scope: Safe-SeqS, specifically the middle-row schematic in the supplied Illumina poster crop: DNA shearing with endogenous molecular identifiers derived from fragment ends, adapter ligation, a combined amplification/solid-phase-capture block, sequencing and family-informed rare-mutation assessment. This is a schematic implementation within the Safe-Sequencing System family, not a statement that every Safe-SeqS protocol uses shearing. The OS-Seq row above and partial Duplex-Seq row below are independent neighboring catalogue schematics; no arrows join them to Safe-SeqS. The left-hand very-rare-mutation icon and explanatory text describe the target and method, rather than an additional preparation branch.

states.label: DNA
features: Biological target: a rare sequence variant in a population of DNA templates, illustrated by an orange mark on a blue double-stranded DNA icon.
The left-hand Very rare mutation graphic is a descriptive target icon. The connected workflow begins at the separate DNA icon; no RNA, cDNA or single-cell partition is depicted.

states.label: Randomly sheared DNA with endogenous molecular identifiers
features: Double-stranded DNA shortened by shearing; the drawing labels its random ends as UMIs.
Endogenous fragment-end identity is the represented molecular identifier; a separately synthesized random barcode is not depicted in this row.
The DNA insert remains the physical carrier of the rare variant.

states.label: Adapter-ligated DNA fragments
features: Sheared DNA insert with added colored terminal adapter segments; the rare variant remains within the insert.

states.label: Amplified DNA library after the solid-phase-capture block
features: Multiple adapter-bearing copies descend from the sheared, adapter-ligated templates; the amplified insert copies represent the original DNA sequences.
The caption explicitly includes solid-phase capture. The support, capture specificity and physical attachment/release state of the drawn output are not illustrated.
Template identity is retained through the fragment ends, while amplification produces multiple descendants for redundant sequencing.

operations.label: Shear
operations.description: Shear the input DNA into shorter fragments. The newly defined random ends supply the endogenous molecular identifiers explicitly labelled in the diagram; the insert sequence, including any pre-existing mutation, remains in the fragment.
operations.mechanism: Physical DNA shearing is stated; the shearing mechanism and end chemistry are not specified.
operations.information_effect: Links a DNA insert and its variant status to a fragment-end identity that can mark descendants of the original template.

operations.label: Adapter ligation
operations.description: Ligate adapters to the sheared DNA fragment ends, producing the illustrated DNA insert flanked by additional colored terminal segments.
operations.mechanism: Adapter ligation is explicitly named; no enzyme or end-group chemistry is identified.
operations.information_effect: Adds library interfaces around the DNA insert while retaining the insert and the shearing-derived template identity.

operations.label: Amplify and solid phase capture
operations.description: Process adapter-ligated fragments through the single depicted Amplify and solid phase capture block, producing a redundant DNA library. The stack depicts increased copy number; capture is named but its substrate selectivity and support are not drawn.
operations.mechanism: Amplification and solid-phase capture remain one broad operation because their internal order and implementation are not resolved by this schematic.
operations.information_effect: Creates multiple descendants carrying the insert sequence and the same inherited fragment-end identity, enabling comparison within template families. The diagram does not establish that every input template is recovered.

operations.label: Align sequences and determine actual ratio
operations.description: Align the sequence reads and determine the depicted actual ratio. operations.mechanism: Computational sequence comparison informed by identifier families; a recurring mutation among descendants is distinguished from sporadic read or amplification errors. The drawing supplies no separate duplex-consensus step.
operations.information_effect: Produces an assessed rare variant and its estimated proportion among represented template molecules. Read redundancy supplies confidence in a template-level mutation; the True mutant label does not guarantee complete specificity or perfect recovery.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local operations apply to the Safe-SeqS middle-row implementation. Its input history is DNA shearing followed by adapter ligation, and the depicted amplification/capture and sequencing instances retain that history. The original-paper abstract identifies Safe-SeqS by UID assignment, UID-family amplification and redundant sequencing, supporting inclusion of this drawing in that assay family. It does not independently establish every depicted preparation detail. Primer-added UID applications in the other papers do not replace this route. The OS-Seq and Duplex-Seq rows have their own titles and arrows and are not alternative branches or aliases of this target.
